intro: You're looking for the best IR35 specialist near you because you want expert help with employment status rules and HMRC compliance. Whether you're a contractor facing an IR35 enquiry or a business engaging contractors, you need someone who understands the complexities and can represent you effectively. We introduce you to UK tax advisers who focus on IR35, so you can get a quote and choose the right professional for your situation.
need_heading: What people searching for an IR35 specialist usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for an IR35 specialist need clear, practical advice on employment status and representation if HMRC comes calling.
needs: You're a contractor who has received an IR35 enquiry letter from HMRC and need representation from someone who knows employment status law.
You're unsure whether your working arrangements fall inside or outside IR35 and want a professional opinion before you sign a contract.
You're a business engaging contractors and need advice on how to assess IR35 status and avoid penalties.
You've been affected by off-payroll working rules in the private or public sector and need help understanding your obligations.
You want to appeal an IR35 decision or negotiate with HMRC, and you need a specialist who has handled similar cases.
context_heading: Understanding IR35 and finding the right specialist
context: IR35 is complex, and HMRC has been actively enforcing compliance. A specialist can help you understand tribunal decisions and how they apply to your situation, but you should ask about their experience with cases like yours.

The term 'tax adviser' is not protected, so qualifications matter. Look for membership of bodies like the Chartered Institute of Taxation (CTA) or the Association of Taxation Technicians (ATT), and ask about their supervision for anti-money-laundering and professional indemnity insurance.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Explain whether you are a contractor, a business engaging contractors, or an intermediary, as this affects the advice you need.
Describe the nature of your work or the contracts you use, including any written terms and working practices.
Mention if you have already received correspondence from HMRC or are facing an enquiry, and what stage it is at.
State whether you need a one-off opinion, ongoing support, or representation in a dispute.
Indicate if you have a preferred location for face-to-face meetings or if remote advice is acceptable.
Share any deadlines or urgent issues so the professional can prioritise your case.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the IR35 specialist
questions: What experience do you have with IR35 cases similar to mine, and can you describe your approach?
Are you a member of the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians?
How do you keep up to date with tribunal decisions and changes to HMRC practice?
Will you represent me directly in discussions with HMRC, or will you work alongside another adviser?
What is your process for assessing IR35 status, and what information will you need from me?
How do you charge for your services, and what is included in your quote?

faqs.q: What should I look for in an IR35 specialist?
faqs.a: Look for a tax adviser with specific experience in employment status and IR35, and check their qualifications and membership of professional bodies. Ask about their track record with similar cases and whether they offer representation.

faqs.q: Can iComply recommend the best IR35 specialist?
faqs.a: We don't rank or endorse professionals. We introduce you to a suitable tax adviser based on your needs, and you can ask questions and compare quotes to decide who is best for you.

faqs.q: How do I know if I'm inside or outside IR35?
faqs.a: IR35 status depends on the specific terms and working practices of your engagement. A specialist can examine your contract and working arrangements to give you an informed opinion.

faqs.q: What happens if HMRC investigates me for IR35?
faqs.a: HMRC will examine your contracts and working practices. A specialist can help you respond, negotiate, and represent you in an appeal or tribunal if necessary.
